name: Unfractionated heparin
executiveSummary: UFH. Adult: bolus **60–80 units/kg** then **12–18 units/kg/h** IV. Pediatrics: bolus **75 units/kg** → **20–28 units/kg/h**. NICU: bolus **75 units/kg** → **28 units/kg/h** titrated to anti-Xa/aPTT. Prophylaxis SC **5000 units every 8–12 h**.
indications:
## Indications

- Treatment/prophylaxis of thromboembolism; ACS; CPB; perioperative bridge.

## Precautions

- Bleeding; HIT. aPTT/anti-Xa every 6 h until stable.
- Not IM. Neuraxial anesthesia: safety intervals.

> Antidote: **protamine** (~1 mg per 100 units recent UFH; common max initial dose 50 mg).

adulto.dose: IV treatment: bolus **80 units/kg** (ACS often **60 units/kg**, common max **4000–5000 units**) → infusion **18 units/kg/h** (ACS **12 units/kg/h**) titrated. Prophylaxis: **5000 units SC every 8–12 h**.
adulto.notes: Line flush (10–100 units/mL) is not a therapeutic dose.

pediatrico.dose: Bolus **75 units/kg** → infusion **20–28 units/kg/h** titrated to anti-Xa/aPTT.

neonatal.dose: Bolus **75 units/kg IV** → infusion **28 units/kg/h**; titrate to anti-Xa (common target **0.3–0.7 units/mL**) — neonatology/hematology.
neonatal.notes: Frequent adjustment due to neonatal clearance.

stability:
## Stability

- Infusion in NS/D5W per compatibility; prepare extemporaneously.
adverseEffects:
## Adverse effects

Bleeding, hematoma, HIT, osteoporosis (chronic), hyperkalemia.
